seen.where: Narvaez, 'Una carta cifrada atribuible a Jose Mariano Michelena (1824)', Estudios de Historia Moderna y Contemporanea de Mexico 41 (2011) pp. 119-133, PDF from redalyc.org/pdf/941/94120769006.pdf (text read, fig. 2 viewed); archive: AHDSREM leg. 40-11-3, no folio numbers.
seen.extent: One letter of 6 Oct 1824 (cryptogram, described in the Calendar of the Hernandez y Davalos collection, Univ. of Texas, Benson); a plain-text sheet of the same message sits in the same legajo.
seen.cipher: Cryptogram not seen directly: the article reproduces a detail of it (fig. 1) and of the plain-text original (fig. 2, a clear Spanish hand text, viewed). Narvaez states the catalogue compilers did not decipher it but drew on the plain-text copy, which precedes the cryptogram in leg. 40-11-3 ('Claves para la correspondencia de la Legacion de Mexico en Inglaterra'). No decipherment of the cryptogram itself is published.

seen.extent: One letter-book page; two telegram copies read here (12 Jan 1874 to Sheridan; 17 Jan 1874 to Maj. G. B. Russell, Austin), each marked 'Official Copy by mail', signed C. C. Augur; the lead records a third on the same page; each about 50-60 words.
seen.cipher: Transcribed as scrambled English word strings with code words (Dresden, Cheyenne, Houston, Waco), e.g. 'Dresden I persons to it fussy unauthorized forward have may self...' and a stray 'Cypher': word transposition with some code words, as the 18 Feb 1869 Grierson letter (Ayer MS 3039) describes for army cypher in Texas. No plaintext or decipherment appears in the transcription.
